note: Ground-truth Q&A set. The benchmark sends each question with EITHER the Markdown or the JSON context and scores exact-match recall against `answer`. Questions are deliberately cross-cutting: they require numbers, nested rules, and combined conditions that are easy to hallucinate.

questions.question: What is the maximum credential TTL for tools exposed to a Tier-2 agent, in seconds?
What status code/tag does a denied call to a non-allowlisted tool return?
What is the maximum CVSS score allowed for known vulnerabilities in a newly introduced dependency?
How many days may a policy exception last at most, and can it be renewed without review?
How long must the full prompt-and-response transcript be retained, in days?
What document ID and version is this policy?
How many AUTHZ_DENIED events for the same tool in one week trigger a registry review?
Which agent tiers are OUT of scope of this policy, and what defining trait do they share?
questions.answer: Tier-1 agents; they have no write access

questions.question: A team wants to give a Tier-2 agent a tool that writes files outside the repo sandbox. What tier is that tool, and what approval does it require?
At how many layers is least privilege enforced, and at which one are unknown parameters rejected?
Who must approve changes to the gateway registry, and via what mechanism?
For an exception, which two roles approve, and can either of them block?
questions.answer: the team's engineering manager and one AppSec reviewer; yes, either may block

questions.question: What must the quarterly red-team exercise include at least one of?
questions.answer: a prompt-injection attempt against a Tier-2 agent

questions.question: What is the effective date of this policy version?
Is the renewal of an expired exception allowed without review, and what happens if a team has an unregistered exception?
questions.answer: No, renewal requires review; an unregistered exception is treated as a policy violation escalated to the CISO office
